post.caption: The first diamond anvils were seized gems. In 1958, a team at the National Bureau of Standards in Washington built the first diamond anvil cell, which squeezes a sample between two gem diamonds. Diamond is the hardest material, and it lets light pass through. The diamonds came from government stock seized by customs agents, and other agencies could have them free if they justified the use. Many anvils broke in testing, and new ones were too costly. In the early 1970s, a speck of ruby joined the cell, and its red glow shifts with pressure, so ruby became the standard gauge.
